study type: secondary analysis of an observational cohort
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 5,325 women who underwent an attempted operative vaginal delivery (3,594 with vacuum and 1,731 with forceps) drawn from a larger primary cohort of 115,502 women.
finding: The duration of operative vaginal delivery may be more strongly associated with adverse neonatal outcomes than the number of vacuum pop-offs or forceps pulls.
mod_finding: The duration of operative vaginal delivery (a mode of birth) is more strongly associated with adverse neonatal outcomes than the number of vacuum pop-offs or forceps pulls.
